original_question: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive or semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature, and let V be the set of appropriate truly flat tangent vectors. Does V determine an integrable subbundle of TX? Can one find a complementary subbundle W with TX = W (+) V? In the semi-positive case, can one construct an MRC fibration f: X -> Y with W = TX/Y? In the semi-negative case, can one construct the Iitaka fibration f: X -> Z associated with K_X with V = TX/Z?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.7 (pp. 1019-1020), motivated by the discussion immediately preceding it after Theorem 3.4: whether the "appropriate" truly flat tangent vectors on a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive (or semi-negative) holomorphic sectional curvature determine an integrable splitting of T_X and recover, respectively, the MRC fibration or the Iitaka fibration.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies the ambient setting of a compact Kähler manifold, the two curvature-sign cases (semi-positive and semi-negative holomorphic sectional curvature), the role of the truly flat tangent vectors V, the integrability question for V, the search for a complementary subbundle W with T_X split as W plus V, and the two sign-specific geometric outputs: an MRC fibration in the semi-positive case and the Iitaka fibration associated with K_X in the semi-negative case. In substance, it is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 3.7.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Problem 3.7 in Section 3, and it is explicitly motivated as a converse to the splitting behavior seen in the proof of Theorem 3.4.
To make the question stand-alone, one should define a truly flat tangent vector: for p in X, a vector v in T_{X,p} is truly flat if R_g(v,x,y,bar z)=0 for all x,y,z in T_{X,p}.

The paper writes V subset T_X as the set of "appropriate" truly flat tangent vectors, with the word "appropriate" left deliberately unspecified; a faithful stand-alone version should preserve that qualifier or note that the paper does not formalize it further, especially for the semi-negative case.

The decomposition should be stated as a direct-sum splitting of the holomorphic tangent bundle, namely T_X isomorphic to W direct-sum V, with W and V understood as holomorphic subbundles if such bundles exist.

Since the identities W = T_{X/Y} and V = T_{X/Z} use relative tangent bundles, the intended fibrations are meant in a form for which these bundles are defined; in the MRC case, the surrounding Section 2 discussion explains that the goal is effectively a holomorphic representative of the MRC fibration.
For full stand-alone clarity, MRC should be expanded once as maximal rationally connected.

The paper's intent in the semi-negative case is not just to identify a splitting, but to use the foliation determined by truly flat vectors to construct the Iitaka fibration and thereby connect to the abundance-conjecture discussion mentioned immediately before Problem 3.7.
refined_question: Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold over C with semi-positive (or semi-negative) holomorphic sectional curvature, and let V subset T_X denote the distribution of "appropriate" truly flat tangent vectors, where a tangent vector v in T_{X,p} is truly flat if R_g(v,x,y,bar z)=0 for all x,y,z in T_{X,p}. Does V define an integrable holomorphic subbundle of T_X, and can one find a holomorphic subbundle W subset T_X such that T_X isomorphic to W direct-sum V? Moreover, in the semi-positive case, can one obtain a holomorphic maximal rationally connected fibration f: X -> Y with W = T_{X/Y}; and in the semi-negative case, can one obtain the Iitaka fibration f: X -> Z associated with K_X with V = T_{X/Z}?
justification: The draft matches Problem 3.7 almost verbatim. The surrounding paragraph explains the intended meaning: in the proof of Theorem 3.4, T_X splits as T_{X/Y} plus pullback(T_Y), the pullback(T_Y) factor is integrable, and all of its tangent vectors are truly flat; Problem 3.7 asks for the converse direction, namely whether truly flat vectors themselves determine the foliation and hence the relevant fibration. Section 2, Lemma 2.2 supplies the foliation-to-morphism mechanism behind the MRC-fibration clause, and the same paragraph before Problem 3.7 ties the semi-negative version to the splitting theorem for the Iitaka fibration and to the abundance-conjecture discussion.
